lines.raw: Front end.
lines.say: Front end.

lines.raw: The **front end** collects the facts a claim will need (who the patient is, who pays, what is covered and approved) and the patient's share, **before** any care is given.
lines.say: The front end collects the facts a claim will need (who the patient is, who pays, what is covered and approved) and the patient's share, before any care is given.

lines.raw: In the US: In the US, the front end is where most denials start.
lines.say: In the U S: In the U S, the front end is where most denials start.

lines.raw: Industry surveys regularly find that **registration and eligibility** problems are among the largest causes of claim denials.
lines.say: Industry surveys regularly find that registration and eligibility problems are among the largest causes of claim denials.

lines.raw: A wrong date of birth, an old insurance card or a missing approval cannot be fixed by good coding later.
lines.say: A wrong date of birth, an old insurance card or a missing approval cannot be fixed by good coding later.

lines.raw: The claim is wrong from the start.
lines.say: The claim is wrong from the start.

lines.raw: Fixing a problem at the front desk takes minutes.
lines.say: Fixing a problem at the front desk takes minutes.

lines.raw: Fixing it after a denial can take weeks and staff time.
lines.say: Fixing it after a denial can take weeks and staff time.

lines.raw: The front-end steps.

lines.raw: Step 1: Scheduling.
lines.say: Step 1: Scheduling.

lines.raw: The patient books a visit.
lines.say: The patient books a visit.

lines.raw: The scheduler records the reason, the doctor and the date, and asks for insurance details.
lines.say: The scheduler records the reason, the doctor and the date, and asks for insurance details.

lines.raw: Step 2: Pre-registration.
lines.say: Step 2: Pre-registration.

lines.raw: Before the visit, staff enter or update the patient's details and insurance, often from a photo of the card.
lines.say: Before the visit, staff enter or update the patient's details and insurance, often from a photo of the card.

lines.raw: Step 3: Insurance check.
lines.say: Step 3: Insurance check.

lines.raw: Staff (or software) ask the insurer: is this person covered on the visit date, and what will they pay?
lines.say: Staff (or software) ask the insurer: is this person covered on the visit date, and what will they pay?

lines.raw: Step 4: Prior authorization check.
lines.say: Step 4: Prior authorization check.

lines.raw: For some expensive services, the insurer must approve in advance.
lines.say: For some expensive services, the insurer must approve in advance.

lines.raw: Staff check whether an approval is needed and on file.
lines.say: Staff check whether an approval is needed and on file.

lines.raw: Step 5: Cost estimate.
lines.say: Step 5: Cost estimate.

lines.raw: The clinic estimates what the patient will owe, using the benefits returned by the insurance check.
lines.say: The clinic estimates what the patient will owe, using the benefits returned by the insurance check.

lines.raw: Step 6: Check-in and collection.
lines.say: Step 6: Check-in and collection.

lines.raw: On the day, the patient confirms details, signs forms and pays the copay or an estimated share.
lines.say: On the day, the patient confirms details, signs forms and pays the copay or an estimated share.

scenes.section: Registration: the facts every claim needs

lines.raw: Registration fields that end up on the claim.
lines.say: Registration fields that end up on the claim.

lines.raw: Patient name and date of birth. Why it matters: The insurer matches the patient by these. Typical error: Nickname instead of legal name; day and month swapped.
lines.say: Patient name and date of birth. Why it matters: The insurer matches the patient by these. Typical error: Nickname instead of legal name; day and month swapped.

lines.raw: Insurance member ID (from the card). Why it matters: Identifies the coverage. Typical error: Old card used after a job change.
lines.say: Insurance member I D (from the card). Why it matters: Identifies the coverage. Typical error: Old card used after a job change.

lines.raw: Subscriber and relationship. Why it matters: Whose plan it is (self, spouse, child). Typical error: Child entered as the subscriber.
lines.say: Subscriber and relationship. Why it matters: Whose plan it is (self, spouse, child). Typical error: Child entered as the subscriber.

lines.raw: Payer and plan. Why it matters: Which insurer to send the claim to. Typical error: Wrong one of two plans with similar names.
lines.say: Payer and plan. Why it matters: Which insurer to send the claim to. Typical error: Wrong one of two plans with similar names.

lines.raw: Other insurance. Why it matters: Decides which plan pays first. Typical error: Second insurance not asked about.
lines.say: Other insurance. Why it matters: Decides which plan pays first. Typical error: Second insurance not asked about.

lines.raw: Guarantor. Why it matters: Who gets the patient statement. Typical error: Bill sent to a parent who is not on file.
lines.say: Guarantor. Why it matters: Who gets the patient statement. Typical error: Bill sent to a parent who is not on file.

lines.raw: The insurance check.
lines.say: The insurance check.

lines.raw: Before the visit, the clinic sends an electronic **eligibility and benefits inquiry** (the **270**, in X12, the standard format for US healthcare electronic transactions) and gets a **271** response back.
lines.say: Before the visit, the clinic sends an electronic eligibility and benefits inquiry (the 2 70, in X12, the standard format for U S healthcare electronic transactions) and gets a 2 71 response back.

lines.raw: It tells the clinic whether the patient is covered on that date and what their copay, deductible and coinsurance are.
lines.say: It tells the clinic whether the patient is covered on that date and what their copay, deductible and coinsurance are.

lines.raw: The **Eligibility** course explains these transactions and the coverage data behind them; here we only use the answer.
lines.say: The Eligibility course explains these transactions and the coverage data behind them; here we only use the answer.

lines.raw: Eligibility owns coverage.
lines.say: Eligibility owns coverage.

lines.raw: Coverage dates, subscribers and dependents, and the 270/271 exchange are taught in the Eligibility course.
lines.say: Coverage dates, subscribers and dependents, and the 2 70/2 71 exchange are taught in the Eligibility course.

lines.raw: For planned scans, surgeries and some drugs, the insurer requires **prior authorization**: approval before the service.
lines.say: For planned scans, surgeries and some drugs, the insurer requires prior authorization: approval before the service.

lines.raw: The front end checks the plan's list and makes sure the approval is requested and on file before the visit.
lines.say: The front end checks the plan's list and makes sure the approval is requested and on file before the visit.

lines.raw: If it is missing, the claim is likely to be denied later.
